## docs/experimental

### docs/experimental/ISO19650_FINDINGS_FROM_NAVISWORKS.md

````markdown
# ISO 19650 Findings — Navisworks Clash Intelligence Platform

**Source repository:** `Aspiring-Design-3D-Consultancy-Ltd/nw-clash-platform` (public)
**Inspected:** 25 Aug 2026 · shallow clone, default branch
**Repo shape:** 96 files — `working.html` (18,585 lines, the entire application), 18 governance markdown docs, 8 `.cline` role definitions, 56 Playwright specs, 2 Node scripts.

---

## 0. Where the ISO 19650 material actually lives

**All of it is in `working.html`.** Nothing else in the repository defines naming conventions, metadata standards, or export rules.

This is worth stating plainly because the task brief expected `docs/governance/` to hold information-delivery specifications. It does not. Those 18 documents govern the *AI engineering workflow* used to build the application — decision logs, investigation logs, workflow routing, release snapshots. Their "role-based" language (`DECISION_LOG.md:24`, `WORKING_AGREEMENTS.md:163`, `.cline/roles/*`) refers to **architect / developer / QA-investigator / release-manager** engineering roles, **not** to ISO 19650 information management roles or RBAC over project information.

Grep confirms the split: `19650` appears **17 times, all in `working.html`**, and zero times in any `.md` file.

Likewise absent from the whole repository: **EIR, BEP, MIDP, TIDP, handover, asset information requirements, COBie, IDS**. `EIR` and `BEP` appear only as prose inside `working.html` — one UI info-box (line 15203) telling the user to align their codes with their EIR and BEP, and two demo clash records citing "BEP §4.2" as a tolerance note. There is no EIR/BEP artefact, template, or data structure.

---

## 1. Naming conventions

### 1.1 The five presets

Defined in the `S.iso.conventions` array (`working.html:829–833`). Every one carries `id`, `name`, `preset`, `separator`, `format`, `description`.

| id | Name | Sep | Format string |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iso19650` | ISO 19650-1:2018 | `_` | `{project}_{originator}_{volume}_{level}_{type}_{disciplines}_{sequence}_{status}_{revision}` |
| `iso19650_date` | ISO 19650-1:2018 + Date | `_` | `{project}_{originator}_{volume}_{level}_{type}_{disciplines}_{sequence}_{status}_{revision}_{date}` |
| `simple` | Simple — Source vs Service | `_` | `[{clashType}]_{sourceA}_vs_{system}_{zone}_{date}` |
| `descriptive` | Descriptive — Full detail | `-` | `{sourceA}-vs-{sourceB}-[{system}]-{zone}-{date}` |
| `uniclass` | Uniclass 2015 | `_` | `{project}_{originator}_{classA}_{classB}_{level}_{sequence}_{date}` |

**Default:** `activeConvention:'iso19650_date'` (line 828) — described in-source as "recommended default".

Presets carry `preset:true` and **cannot be deleted or edited** in the UI; only custom conventions get Edit/✕ controls. Deleting the active custom convention falls back to `iso19650_date` (line 15677).

### 1.2 Token vocabulary — 19 tokens

`{project}` `{originator}` `{volume}` `{level}` `{type}` `{disciplines}` `{disciplineA}` `{disciplineB}` `{sequence}` `{status}` `{revision}` `{date}` `{sourceA}` `{sourceB}` `{system}` `{zone}` `{clashType}` `{classA}` `{classB}`

Substitution is a naive global regex replace per key (`applyConvFormat`, ~line 7300): unmatched tokens resolve to empty string, so a malformed format silently yields a name with empty segments.

> **Gap worth noting:** the Uniclass 2015 convention is offered, but `classA` and `classB` are **hardcoded to empty strings** in the value map (`genTestName`, line ~7274: `classA:'',classB:''`). Selecting Uniclass therefore produces a name with two empty segments. The convention is present in the UI but not actually wired to any classification data. There is no Uniclass or OmniClass code table anywhere in the repo.

### 1.3 Base codes (the `S.iso` object, line 827)

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `projCode` | empty (required, e.g. `A1234`) | Unique project identifier |
| `origCode` | empty (required, e.g. `BIM01`) | Author / issuing organisation |
| `typeCode` | `CO` | Information type |
| `suitability` | `S1` | CDE status |
| `revision` | `01` | `P01` = preliminary, `C01` = contract |
| `separator` | `_` | `_` or `-` (custom conventions also allow `.`) |

**Type codes:** `CO` Coordination · `RP` Report · `MO` Model.

### 1.4 Master code library

`ISO_MASTER_CODES` (line 852) is explicitly commented *"never modified — project codes are separate"*. Projects select from it or add custom codes scoped to that project only.

- **Disciplines (12):** S Structural · M MEP/Mechanical · A Architectural · E Electrical · C Civil · F Fire Protection · G Geotechnical · L Landscape · I Interior Design · P Public Health/Plumbing · T Telecommunications · X External Works
- **Volumes (9):** ZZ Multi-system/All · 10 Structural Frame · 20 Architectural · 30 MEP Services · 40 Electrical · 50 Civil/External · 60 Façade/Envelope · 70 Infrastructure · XX Not applicable
- **Levels (18):** ZZ All · B03–B01 Basements · G00 Ground · M00 Mezzanine · L01–L10 · RF Roof · XX Not applicable

Cited in the UI as *ISO 19650-1 §12, Annex A*.

### 1.5 CDE status codes — "ISO 19650-2 Table 1"

Rendered as a 7-row reference grid (line ~15278), each mapped to a platform status:

| Code | Meaning | Platform status | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S0` | Work in progress | New | `#94A3B8` |
| `S1` | Suitable for coordination | Active | `#FF8000` |
| `S2` | Suitable for information | Reviewed | `#00AEEF` |
| `S3` | Suitable for review | — | `#2563EB` |
| `A` | Authorised for use | Approved | `#00B050` |
| `B` | Partially authorised | — | `#FFC000` |
| `S7` | Archived / superseded | Resolved | `#6B7280` |

Only `S0 S1 S2 S3 A` are selectable in the Suitability dropdown; `B` and `S7` appear in the reference table only.

### 1.6 Date formats

Five options in the name generator: `YYMMDD` (default) · `DDMMYY` · `YYYYMMDD` · `DD-MM-YY` · `ISO` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

### 1.7 Dual output

`genTestName()` emits **two** names simultaneously:

- **ISO name** — the convention applied, for information containers and BCF export
- **Navisworks label** — informal, `[H] SourceA vs SourceB [System] Zone YYMMDD`, where the type tag is `[H]` Hard · `[CL]` Clearance · `[DUP]` Duplicate

The `simple` convention is explicitly annotated *"not ISO compliant"* — it exists for Navisworks test names, which have their own practical constraints.

---

## 2. Metadata requirements

### 2.1 BCF 2.1 topic metadata

Consistent across all six BCF writer sites (lines 6847, 12704, 13256, 13272, 13353, 17489):

| Field | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Topic@Guid` | yes | generated GUID |
| `Topic@TopicType` | yes | always `Clash` |
| `Topic@TopicStatus` | yes | clash status |
| `Title` | yes | `<UID> — <name>` |
| `Priority` | yes | defaults `Medium` |
| `CreationDate` | yes | ISO 8601 + `+00:00` |
| `CreationAuthor` | yes | `bcfAuthor()` |
| `Description` | yes | disciplines, elements, element IDs, penetration in mm |
| `AssignedTo` | conditional | **omitted entirely when blank** |
| `Labels/Label` | group exports only | group name |
| `Viewpoints/ViewPoint` | yes | `viewpoint.bcfv` + snapshot |

A source comment at line 12590 records that `CreationAuthor` is *"REQUIRED by BCF 2.1 spec"* and was previously missing — a fixed defect. A second comment (line 17487) records empty `IfcGuid` attributes as an **XSD violation**; `Components` are written with `IfcGuid=""` and the Navisworks element ID in `AuthoringToolId` instead, because Navisworks XML carries no IFC GUIDs.

### 2.2 Element identity attributes

`working.html:7544` defines the element-ID attribute resolution order, built from field incidents:

```
['Element ID', 'GUID', '要素ID', '要素 ID', '元素 ID', 'Entity Handle']
```

Covering English, Japanese and Chinese Navisworks installs plus AutoCAD entity handles. `.idSrc` records which attribute actually yielded the value.

### 2.3 Clash register fields (CSV export, line 17469)

```
ID, Name, Test, Discipline A, Discipline B, Element A, Element B,
Penetration, Status, Priority, Assigned To, Notes, Date
```

### 2.4 Project-level metadata

`project.bcfp` carries only `ProjectId` (GUID) + `Name`. Application state holds `projName` and `projWeek` — no client, no location, no contract reference.

---

## 3. Export standards

| Export | Format | Filename pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Clash register | CSV | `ClashRegister_<date>.csv` |
| Issues | BCF 2.1 ZIP | ISO name from active convention |
| Group issues | ZIP | `<primaryTestName> Groups.zip` |
| Report | HTML | `<projName>_Report_<date>.html` |
| Weekly report | HTML | `<projName>_WeeklyReport_<date>.html` |
| Slides | PPTX | — |
| Backup | JSON | — |

`projName` is sanitised with `replace(/[^\w]/g,'_')`.

**BCF 2.1 container structure:** `bcf.version` (`VersionId="2.1"`, `DetailedVersion 2.1`, `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="version.xsd"`) · `project.bcfp` · then per-topic GUID folders holding `markup.bcf`, `viewpoint.bcfv`, `snapshot.png`.

Stated interoperability target (About box, line 15420): **BIMCollab Zoom, Autodesk BIM Collaborate, Revit native BCF plugins**.

**No IFC export exists** — the platform consumes Navisworks Clash Detective XML and emits BCF/CSV/PPTX/PDF/HTML. There is no IFC naming standard setting anywhere in the repo.

---

## 4. Role and permission framework

`working.html:876–905`. This is genuine RBAC over application actions — the only RBAC in the repository.

**Four roles, ranked:**

| Role | Label | Rank |
|---|---|---|
| `admin` | Administrator | 4 |
| `manager` | Space Planning Manager | 3 |
| `projectManager` | Project Manager | 2 |
| `viewer` | Viewer | 1 |

**Thirteen permissions**, each a minimum rank:

| Permission | Min rank |
|---|---|
| `data_manager`, `settings_full`, `role_management` | 4 — Admin only |
| `edit_register`, `import_xml`, `bcf_tools`, `add_clash`, `export_csv`, `export_bcf`, `settings_project`, `board_move`, `edit_notes` | 3 — Manager+ |
| `export_reports` | 2 — Project Manager+ |

Enforced by `can(perm)` (rank comparison) and `applyRoleUI()`, which hides any element carrying `data-minrole` and re-renders toolbar actions. Viewers see a read-only notice: *"Read-only access — contact your BIM Coordinator to make changes"*.

Authentication is a 4-digit PIN, SHA-256 hashed, stored in browser `localStorage`.

---

## 5. Compliance claim and its limits

The About box (line 15417) claims compliance with **BS EN ISO 19650-1:2018** and **BS EN ISO 19650-2:2018** *information container naming conventions* — scoped to naming, not to the standard as a whole. That scoping is accurate to what is implemented.

**Present:** naming conventions, code libraries, CDE status mapping, BCF 2.1 metadata, RBAC.

**Absent:** EIR/BEP artefacts · MIDP/TIDP delivery planning · handover / asset information requirements · document classification taxonomy (Uniclass tokens exist but resolve empty) · COBie · IDS · any IFC naming standard · federation strategy · security-mindedness (ISO 19650-5).

---

## 6. What was carried into BIMGUARD

The BIMGUARD **Settings → ISO 19650 Compliance** section reproduces, as configurable fields: the five naming conventions and their format strings, the 19-token vocabulary, the base-code fields, the type/suitability/revision code sets, the discipline/volume/level master library counts, the CDE status table, the BCF 2.1 metadata field lists, the export filename patterns, and the four-role permission matrix.

Three fields are **BIMGUARD additions, not found in the Navisworks repo**, and are labelled as such in the UI: the IFC naming standard dropdown, the information delivery plan template, and the document classification taxonomy. BIMGUARD is IFC-native where the Navisworks platform is not, so an IFC naming setting has somewhere to attach here; the other two fill gaps section 5 identifies.
````

## docs/ISO19650

### docs/ISO19650/BIMGuard-ISO19650-Requirements.md

```markdown
# **Software Requirements Specification: ISO 19650 Compliance Engine for BIM-Guard**

## **Architectural Context and Baseline System Assessment**

The open-source platform BIM-Guard provides automated code compliance auditing, OpenBIM model inspection, and regulatory rule extraction[^1]. Its software architecture is organized around a decoupled service paradigm consisting of a Python FastAPI backend operating as an Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) service and a Single-Page Application (SPA) frontend built with Vite, Svelte 5, and Tailwind CSS[^2]. The underlying parsing and validation core relies on IfcOpenShell for Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) processing, buildingSMART Information Delivery Specification (IDS) evaluation, the buildingSMART Data Dictionary (bSDD) REST client, and the ThatOpenCompany Web-IFC viewport for geometric visualization[^2]. Persistence, relational integrity, and document storage are managed via Supabase PostgreSQL, which utilizes Row-Level Security (RLS) policies[^2]. Automated rule generation leverages LiteLLM across multiple foundation model providers, supported by web retrieval mechanisms[^2].

While BIM-Guard possesses analytical capabilities for domain-specific engineering checks—such as seismic clearance validation (GC-001) and atmospheric pipe corrosion risk assessment (CC-001)[^2]—it currently functions as an isolated quality gate rather than an integrated information management environment[^2]. To transition into full compliance with the ISO 19650 standard series ("Organization and digitization of information about buildings and civil engineering works, including building information modelling (BIM) — Information management using building information modelling"), the platform must expand its functional boundaries[^4]. This requires adopting the structured management processes defined across ISO 19650-1 (Concepts and Principles), ISO 19650-2 (Delivery Phase of Assets), ISO 19650-4 (Information Exchange), and ISO 19650-5 (Security-Minded Approach to Information Management)[^4].

The transition demands that BIM-Guard evolve from an ad-hoc checker into an authoritative digital delivery gatekeeper capable of enforcing Common Data Environment (CDE) state machines, multi-tier information exchange verification, decoupled metadata integrity, and entity-level access security[^3].

| Standard Subsystem           | Target ISO 19650 Clause     | BIM-Guard Baseline Capability                                                                              | Target Compliant State                                                                                                                               |
| :--------------------------- | :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CDE Workflow States**      | ISO 19650-1 §12[^3]         | Unmanaged flat storage within Supabase buckets; project-wide file lists without lifecycle segregation[^2]. | Four discrete, access-controlled information states (WIP, SHARED, PUBLISHED, ARCHIVED) governed by verifiable transition gates[^3].                  |
| **Container Identification** | ISO 19650-2 §NA.1–NA.3[^11] | Arbitrary file upload naming with optional client-side string patterns[^2].                                | Strict enforcement of standard 7-field convention with delimiter validation, custom field lengths, and automated rejection[^11].                     |
| **Metadata Management**      | ISO 19650-2 §NA.4[^11]      | Metadata conflated with file names; basic revision timestamps[^2].                                         | Complete decoupling of container identifiers from lifecycle metadata (suitability codes, multi-tier revision identifiers) stored in PostgreSQL[^11]. |
| **Exchange Verification**    | ISO 19650-4 §5.1–§5.6[^15]  | Unstructured pass/fail rule execution targeting selected physical properties[^2].                          | Formal four-tier evaluation pipeline (Syntactic, Schema, Semantic, Pragmatic) generating authoritative disposition statuses[^8].                     |
| **Collaboration Interfaces** | ISO 19650-4 §6[^8]          | Static BCF report export[^2].                                                                              | Full bidirectional openCDE Foundation API and BCF REST API v3.0 endpoints synchronizing topics with external CDE platforms[^2].                      |
| **Security Governance**      | ISO 19650-5 §5–§8[^9]       | Basic project-level Supabase RLS authentication[^2].                                                       | Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), security triage workflows, dynamic IFC geometric and semantic redaction, and SHA-256 audit chaining[^9].      |

## **Information Container Identification and Metadata Specification (ISO 19650-2)**

ISO 19650-2 mandates that every distinct information container maintained within a CDE—such as IFC models, drawing packages, calculation sheets, and specification documents—possess a unique identification string defined by an agreed project naming convention[^3]. A critical defect in historical information management implementations has been the embedding of transient lifecycle attributes (such as approval status and revision indexes) within the physical file name[^11]. This practice results in broken hyperlinks, orphaned file dependencies, and synchronization failures across distributed federated systems[^4]. In full compliance with ISO 19650-2, BIM-Guard enforces the absolute decoupling of container identifiers from operational metadata[^11]. The physical container name remains immutable across its operational lifespan, while revisions, status codes, and classifications are managed exclusively through database-backed metadata schemas[^11].

The file naming engine implements the widely adopted National Annex standard structure, requiring seven distinct fields delimited strictly by a hyphen-minus character (-)[^11]. Under this standard, internal field values must not contain punctuation marks, spaces, symbols, or underscores[^12].

| Field Number | Field Name           | Purpose and Definition                                                    | Allowed Length | Character Set           | Standard Codification Examples                    |
| :----------- | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| **Field 1**  | Project              | Unique project code established in the Project Information Standard[^11]. | 2 to 6         | Alphanumeric ([A-Z0-9]) | PRJ001, BLD77                                     |
| **Field 2**  | Originator           | Unique code identifying the authoring organization[^11].                  | 3 to 6         | Alphanumeric ([A-Z0-9]) | ARUP, MOTTS, MAIC                                 |
| **Field 3**  | Functional Breakdown | Functional volume or system spatial boundary[^11].                        | 2              | Alphanumeric ([A-Z0-9]) | 01, ZZ (All), XX (None)                           |
| **Field 4**  | Spatial Breakdown    | Specific level, location, or vertical subdivision[^11].                   | 2              | Alphanumeric ([A-Z0-9]) | GF (Ground), 01, ZZ (All)                         |
| **Field 5**  | Form                 | Structural type or presentation form of information[^11].                 | 2              | Alphabetic ([A-Z])      | M3 (3D Model), DR (Drawing), VS (Visual)[^11]     |
| **Field 6**  | Discipline           | Technical discipline responsible for the information[^11].                | 1 to 2         | Alphabetic ([A-Z])      | A (Architect), S (Structure), M (Mechanical)[^11] |
| **Field 7**  | Number               | Sequential integer disambiguating otherwise identical profiles[^11].      | 4 to 6         | Numeric ([0-9])         | 0001, 010042                                      |

The metadata attached to each container in the Supabase PostgreSQL data store must track the exact status and revision history without altering the stored container key[^2]. The revision numbering engine enforces a strict two-tier syntax[^11]. During preliminary iterations within the Work in Progress state, the revision is formatted as Pnn.nn, where P signifies preliminary, the first two integer digits denote the target formal revision, and the two suffix digits represent internal task-team development cycles (for example, P01.01)[^2]. When a container successfully traverses the verification gate into the Shared state, the internal suffix is dropped, locking the revision identifier to Pnn (such as P01)[^6]. If the container is subsequently authorized for contractual publication, the revision prefix transitions to Cnn (such as C01), signifying contractual baseline validity[^11].

Suitability codes reflect the specific authorized business use of the container and are constrained by the container's active state[^11]. The system permits status codes S1 through S5 exclusively within the Shared state[^11]. Specifically, S1 authorizes the container for coordination across design disciplines, S2 provides information for reference only, S3 designates submission for multidisciplinary review and comment, S4 signals formal submission for lead appointed party stage approval, and S5 indicates submission for appointing party acceptance[^11]. Within the Published state, only contractual codes are permitted, including A1 through An (indicating authorization for construction stages, regulatory sign-off, or procurement) and B1 through Bn (indicating partial sign-off with non-blocking reservations)[^11]. Containers situated within Work in Progress are restricted to the default non-authorized code S0[^11].

| Database Column Name | Data Type   | Constraint and Validation Rules                                  | ISO 19650-2 Semantic Mapping                          |
| :------------------- | :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------- |
| container_id         | UUID        | Primary Key, gen_random_uuid()                                   | Unique container entity identifier[^3].               |
| file_name            | TEXT        | Unique, enforces 7-field hyphenated regex pattern                | Immutable physical container identifier[^11].         |
| cde_state            | VARCHAR(20) | CHECK (cde_state IN ('WIP', 'SHARED', 'PUBLISHED', 'ARCHIVED'))  | Active information state[^3].                         |
| suitability_code     | VARCHAR(3)  | Validated against active state constraints (S0–S5, A1–An, B1–Bn) | Purpose of issue and authorized operational use[^11]. |
| revision_code        | VARCHAR(8)  | Enforces regex `^(Pd{2}(.d{2})?                                  | Cd{2})$`                                              |
| classification_uri   | TEXT        | Must resolve to valid buildingSMART Data Dictionary URI          | Semantic domain categorization (Uniclass 2015)[^2].   |
| sha256_hash          | CHAR(64)    | Exact hex-encoded SHA-256 binary digest                          | Cryptographic payload integrity verification.         |
| author_id            | UUID        | Foreign Key to auth.users                                        | Originating actor tracking and non-repudiation[^3].   |

## **Common Data Environment Workflow and Gated State Machine Controls**

ISO 19650-1 and ISO 19650-2 establish that an information container must reside within exactly one of four discrete CDE workflow states at any point in its existence[^3]. Progression between these states is governed by formal transition gates that prevent unauthorized dissemination and enforce explicit verification, approval, and authorization steps[^3].

The lifecycle begins in the Work in Progress (WIP) state, which represents the private drafting domain of a specific appointed task team[^3]. Here, information is authored and iterated without exposing intermediate design discrepancies to external project participants[^3]. Status codes are locked to S0, and revision numbering progresses through internal increments (P01.01, P01.02)[^2]. Task team members maintain read, write, and soft-deletion permissions within their isolated tenancy[^3]. External project participants, including the lead appointed party and appointing party, are barred from accessing WIP containers[^3].

Transition Gate 1 (Check / Review / Approve) mediates the boundary between Work in Progress and the Shared state[^3]. To initiate Gate 1 promotion, the originating task team submits the container to BIM-Guard's automated pre-flight gateway[^2]. The orchestrator validates file naming conformity, schema integrity, and initial Level of Information Need compliance[^2]. Upon passing these automated checks, the task team lead must digitally record an approval event, which generates a cryptographic log entry[^3]. BIM-Guard then advances the container state to SHARED, increments the revision metadata to the formal preliminary issue (dropping the decimal suffix to yield P01), and assigns an appropriate suitability code (typically S1 for coordination or S2 for information)[^6].

The Shared state serves as the collaborative coordination plane[^3]. Here, information is accessible to all appointed project participants to enable multi-disciplinary federation, clash detection, and engineering reviews[^3]. Containers in the Shared state remain non-contractual[^11]. Permissions for all appointed participants are strictly read-only; editing or direct overwriting of shared containers is prohibited[^3]. If a task team must rectify a coordination defect identified in the Shared state, the container is not modified in place; instead, a new revision cycle is initialized in WIP (for instance, P02.01), leaving the historical Shared record intact[^6].

Transition Gate 2 (Authorize / Accept) governs the progression from the Shared state to the Published state[^3]. This milestone signifies that the coordinated information delivery has undergone complete multidisciplinary federation, clash resolution, and compliance evaluation[^3]. The Lead Appointed Party verifies that the deliverables fulfill the Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP), while the Appointing Party formally accepts the deliverable against the project Exchange Information Requirements (EIR)[^4]. BIM-Guard executes comprehensive automated compliance auditing—including spatial code rules, material durability algorithms, and full IDS validation[^2]. When all criteria pass and formal digital authorization is recorded, the container transitions to PUBLISHED[^3]. Its revision rolls to contractual status (C01), and its suitability code transitions to a definitive stage purpose (such as A1 or A2)[^11].

The Published state contains authorized, legally binding project outputs used for statutory approvals, procurement, fabrication, and physical construction[^3]. Immutability is enforced at the database and object-storage tiers: PostgreSQL triggers reject any update or deletion queries targeting published records[^2]. When an asset lifecycle stage concludes, or when a published deliverable is superseded by an authorized design alteration, the container moves across Gate 3 into the Archived state[^3]. Archiving maintains an immutable historical audit record, providing a forensic trail for post-occupancy dispute resolution, legal defensibility, and long-term asset management in accordance with ISO 19650-3[^3].

| State Name                 | Allowed Outbound State Transitions                                     | Permitted Suitability Codes                    | Permitted Revision Formats                     | Access Control and Authority Profiles                                                               | Immutability Constraints                               |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------- |
| **Work in Progress (WIP)** | Transition to SHARED (via Gate 1 approval)[^3].                        | S0 exclusively[^11].                           | Pnn.nn (e.g., P01.01, P01.02)[^2].             | Authoring Task Team: Read, Write, Delete[^3]. All other project actors: Denied[^3].                 | Mutable. Versions track internal progress[^6].         |
| **Shared**                 | Revert to WIP (upon rejection); Advance to PUBLISHED (via Gate 2)[^3]. | S1, S2, S3, S4, S5[^11].                       | Pnn (e.g., P01, P02)[^6].                      | Appointed Parties: Read Only[^3]. Lead Appointed Party: Read, Review, Authorize[^3].                | Immutable. In-place file mutations rejected[^3].       |
| **Published**              | Transition to ARCHIVED (via Gate 3 supersession)[^3].                  | A1 through An, B1 through Bn[^11].             | Cnn (e.g., C01, C02)[^11].                     | All Project Parties: Read Only[^3]. Appointing Party: Read, Audit[^3].                              | Strictly Immutable. Blocked via database triggers[^2]. |
| **Archived**               | Terminal state; no outbound state transitions[^3].                     | Retains historical code at archival point[^3]. | Retains historical code at archival point[^3]. | Appointing Party and Legal Auditors: Read Only[^3]. All other parties: Access revoked or read-only. | Strictly Immutable. Indefinite preservation[^3].       |

## **Information Exchange, Verification, and Validation Framework (ISO 19650-4)**

ISO 19650-4 introduces a formal methodology for executing and evaluating information exchanges across the asset lifecycle[^7]. The standard draws an essential distinction between verification and validation[^7]. Verification evaluates whether the technical payload of an information container adheres to defined syntax, schema, file structure, and standardized codification rules[^7]. Validation evaluates whether the informational content satisfies the specific operational, geometric, and semantic requirements defined by the appointing party for a particular delivery milestone[^7].

BIM-Guard executes automated information exchange evaluations via a four-tier processing pipeline[^2]. This pipeline runs asynchronously upon container ingestion and produces verifiable metrics that directly govern CDE gate clearances[^2].

| Evaluation Tier                           | Functional Classification | Technical Mechanism and Engines                                                                                                                        | Deterministic Pass/Fail Criteria                                                                                                  | Applicable Standards                            |
| :---------------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------- |
| **Tier 1: Syntactic Integrity**           | Verification              | Low-level lexical parser evaluating ISO 10303-21 STEP physical file grammar, schema version header (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4.3), and GUID string syntax[^2]. | Zero parsing syntax errors; exact 22-character base64 GUID formatting across all entity records; single project root element[^2]. | ISO 10303-21, ISO 16739-1, ISO 19650-4 §5.2[^8] |
| **Tier 2: Schema & Delivery Spec**        | Verification              | Automated execution of buildingSMART Information Delivery Specification (IDS 1.0) XML contracts using ifcopenshell.ids[^2].                            | All mandatory entity, classification, material, property, and relation facets resolve within tolerance thresholds[^2].            | buildingSMART IDS 1.0, ISO 19650-4 §5.3[^8]     |
| **Tier 3: Semantic Conformance**          | Verification & Validation | Automated resolution of classification parameters and property set dictionaries via the buildingSMART Data Dictionary REST API[^2].                    | Property set assignments, data types, and enumeration values conform to official bSDD domain definitions[^2].                     | ISO 12006-3, ISO 19650-4 §5.4[^8]               |
| **Tier 4: Engineering & Code Compliance** | Validation                | Native BIM-Guard physics and regulatory engines: GC-001 (seismic bracing clearances) and CC-001 (corrosion galvanic compatibility)[^2].                | Zero non-exempt physical clashes, structural clearance violations, or galvanic degradation hazards[^2].                           | ASCE 7-22, ISO 9223, ISO 19650-4 §5.5[^2]       |

The cumulative outcomes across all four tiers determine the formal exchange decision disposition[^15]. If Tier 1 or critical Tier 2 IDS checks detect defects, the exchange is designated as REJECTED[^8]. The container is quarantined within WIP, promotion across Gate 1 is halted, and an exportable BCF topic archive is compiled[^2]. If all Tier 1 and Tier 2 criteria are satisfied, but Tier 3 or Tier 4 checks flag non-critical warnings, the exchange is categorized as ACCEPTED_WITH_COMMENTS[^8]. Under this status, the container advances to the target state, but tracking issues are registered via the BCF REST API, requiring resolution before the subsequent milestone[^2]. When all checks pass without exceptions, the exchange achieves an ACCEPTED status, clearing the container for progression across the active gate[^3].

To facilitate multi-disciplinary issue resolution, every detected non-conformance is transformed into a structured BCF v3.0 topic[^2]. The engine extracts the camera viewpoint, orthogonal clipping planes, and globally unique identifiers (GUIDs) of failing IFC entities directly from the model[^2]. It attaches the precise clause violation report, classification reference, and required remediation instructions, allowing lead designers to pull the issue context directly into desktop authoring software[^2].

## **Security-Minded Information Management Architecture (ISO 19650-5)**

ISO 19650-5 establishes principles for safeguarding sensitive digital engineering data against compromise, loss, and unauthorized dissemination[^9]. Digital models of built assets frequently incorporate Sensitive Commercial Information (SCI) or Sensitive Security Information (SSI), such as the layout of critical building utilities, telecommunications nodes, detention areas, secure vaults, and perimeter surveillance systems[^9]. In accordance with ISO 19650-5, BIM-Guard implements a comprehensive security governance framework combining security triage, Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), runtime geometric and semantic redaction, and an immutable cryptographic audit ledger[^9].

The security triage engine evaluates containers and internal IFC model structures during ingestion, assigning appropriate security clearance thresholds based on project security plans[^17].

| Security Classification                | Information Scope and Asset Typology                                                                                         | Technical Access Restriction Mechanism                                                      | Authorized Project Roles                                              |
| :------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1: Public / Open**             | Architectural massing, general exterior envelopes, published planning submittals[^9].                                        | Unrestricted authenticated read access; visible in common federation models[^3].            | All authenticated project users and public stakeholders[^3].          |
| **Level 2: Commercial Sensitive**      | Bill of quantities, unit cost schedules, contractor trade pricing, proprietary equipment specifications[^9].                 | Attribute-level masking within the API; stripped from non-commercial federated exports[^2]. | Appointing Party, Commercial Lead, Quantity Surveyors[^4].            |
| **Level 3: Infrastructure Restricted** | Primary MEP risers, high-voltage distribution networks, primary structural load transfer joints[^9].                         | Model segregation; access granted strictly via project role assignment[^9].                 | Lead Appointed Party, Appointed Lead Engineers[^4].                   |
| **Level 4: High Security Restricted**  | Security operations centers, access control circuits, custodial locks, executive protection zones, detention perimeters[^9]. | Dynamic geometric and semantic redaction via IfcOpenShell streaming filter[^2].             | Appointing Party Security Manager and Vetted Security Task Teams[^4]. |

When a project participant accesses an IFC container via direct file download or streams it into the Web-IFC viewer, BIM-Guard's sanitization service checks the user's cryptographic security clearance against the sensitivity tagging of the model elements[^2]. If a user lacking Level 4 clearance requests a model containing restricted entities, the service sanitizes the payload on the fly[^2]. The streaming pipeline prunes the associated IfcProduct entities, removes their geometric representations from the product tree, strips sensitive property sets (such as Pset_SecurityProperties), and unlinks related relationship records (IfcRelDefinesByProperties, IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure)[^2]. This guarantees that unauthorized users receive a structurally and coordinate-consistent IFC model for coordination without exposing protected architectural layouts[^3].

To enforce non-repudiation and meet regulatory auditing requirements, every container transaction—including uploads, gate evaluations, streaming sessions, redactions, and file downloads—is recorded in an append-only audit ledger[^3]. Each log entry captures the timestamp, authenticated actor identifier, source IP address, action performed, and the SHA-256 binary hash of the affected payload[^3]. The ledger secures the sequence of operations by calculating each record's hash from its own content combined with the hash of the preceding entry, producing a tamper-evident audit chain that invalidates any retroactive administrative database tampering[^17].

## **Functional Requirements**

The following tables define the functional requirements necessary to achieve full ISO 19650 compliance within the BIM-Guard platform.

### **Information Container Identification (FR-01)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification       | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Implementation Target                                                                                                       |
| :------------- | :------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **FR-01.1**    | Container Delimiter Enforcement | The system must validate that the information container name contains exactly six hyphen-minus delimiters (-), separating exactly seven naming fields[^11]. File extensions must be separated exclusively by a final period[^12]. | Ingestion engine parses file name; any name utilizing underscores, spaces, or extra hyphens is rejected with HTTP 422[^12]. |
| **FR-01.2**    | Project Field Code Validation   | Field 1 of the container name must match an active, registered project identifier code defined within the project configuration table[^2].                                                                                        | File name validation fails if Field 1 does not exist in public.projects.code[^2].                                           |
| **FR-01.3**    | Field Character Set Conformance | Each field must adhere to its authorized alphanumeric character sets and character length constraints as defined by the project Information Standard[^11].                                                                        | Regex validation fails on special characters or length boundary violations[^11].                                            |
| **FR-01.4**    | Configurable Naming Schema      | The system must allow project administrators to modify field lengths, permitted discipline codes, and form codifications per project[^11].                                                                                        | Schema definitions maintained in project_naming_standards table and evaluated dynamically.                                  |
| **FR-01.5**    | Automated File Sanitization     | The ingestion pipeline must reject files containing non-ASCII characters, trailing spaces, or reserved URI escape characters[^12].                                                                                                | System returns structured error detailing offending byte sequences and characters.                                          |

### **CDE Workflow and Gated State Machine Controls (FR-02)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification     | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                                                | Implementation Target                                                                                         |
| :------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **FR-02.1**    | Initial State Allocation      | All newly uploaded information containers must be initialized strictly to the WORK_IN_PROGRESS (WIP) state[^3].                                                | Direct creation of containers in Shared or Published states is blocked.                                       |
| **FR-02.2**    | Automated Gate 1 Clearance    | Transition of a container from WIP to SHARED must require passing Tier 1 and Tier 2 validation checks alongside task team lead digital sign-off[^2].           | Endpoint /api/cde/gate1/promote returns HTTP 400 if validation findings contain critical errors[^2].          |
| **FR-02.3**    | Gate 2 Milestone Clearance    | Transition of a container from SHARED to PUBLISHED must require Lead Appointed Party authorization and passing all Tier 3 and Tier 4 EIR checks[^2].           | Promotion endpoint verifies digital signature of authorized role and checks for zero blocking BCF topics[^2]. |
| **FR-02.4**    | Published Record Immutability | Containers in the PUBLISHED state must be immutable at both the database and object storage layers[^2]. Modifications require creating a new WIP revision[^6]. | Database trigger prevents UPDATE or DELETE operations on published container records[^2].                     |
| **FR-02.5**    | Archival Supersession Logic   | Advancing a container to a new contractual revision in PUBLISHED must automatically update the previous revision's state to ARCHIVED[^3].                      | Transition triggers automatic lifecycle state update and audit log generation[^3].                            |

### **Metadata and Revision Governance (FR-03)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification       | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                            | Implementation Target                                                                             |
| :------------- | :------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **FR-03.1**    | Decoupled Metadata Persistence  | Container revision, suitability code, and classification must be stored exclusively in database fields, leaving file names immutable[^11]. | System retains the exact file upload name in storage buckets while updating metadata columns[^2]. |
| **FR-03.2**    | State-Constrained Suitability   | Suitability codes must be validated against the active container state (S0 in WIP; S1–S5 in Shared; A1–An, B1–Bn in Published)[^11].       | Assignment of unauthorized suitability codes rejected with HTTP 400 and validation error[^11].    |
| **FR-03.3**    | Revision Progression Automation | Revisions must enforce Pnn.nn within WIP, normalize to Pnn upon Gate 1 promotion, and roll to Cnn upon Gate 2 publication[^6].             | Version engine increments minor version on re-upload and updates format upon gate traversal[^6].  |
| **FR-03.4**    | Semantic Classification Linking | Every container must link to a valid classification identifier verified against the buildingSMART Data Dictionary[^2].                     | URI validation confirms presence in Uniclass 2015, OmniClass, or project dictionary[^2].          |

### **Automated Information Verification and Validation (FR-04)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification     | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                                  | Implementation Target                                                                            |
| :------------- | :---------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **FR-04.1**    | Syntactic & Schema Parsing    | The system must validate IFC files against ISO 10303-21 syntax and buildingSMART schemas (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4.3) using IfcOpenShell[^2].          | Syntax failures halt processing immediately and mark container as REJECTED[^2].                  |
| **FR-04.2**    | IDS 1.0 Automated Auditing    | The platform must execute project IDS XML specifications against uploaded models, testing entity, property, and classification facets[^2].       | System generates structured JSON audit results and logs passing percentage metrics[^2].          |
| **FR-04.3**    | bSDD Terminology Verification | Classification references, property set definitions, and units must be validated against the bSDD API, with fallback to local cache[^2].         | Unresolved classification URIs or invalid data types generate Tier 3 validation warnings[^2].    |
| **FR-04.4**    | Automated BCF 3.0 Reporting   | All validation failures and spatial clashes must generate BCF topics containing camera coordinates, component GUIDs, and error descriptions[^2]. | Exportable BCF 3.0 archive and REST endpoints populated automatically upon audit completion[^2]. |

### **Security-Minded Information Governance (FR-05)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification   | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                                     | Implementation Target                                                                             |
| :------------- | :-------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **FR-05.1**    | Security Triage and Tagging | System must provide administrative interfaces to tag containers, spatial zones, or IFC element classes with security clearance levels[^9].          | Security metadata persisted in cde_information_containers and related entity tables[^2].          |
| **FR-05.2**    | Dynamic Entity Redaction    | The streaming parser must redact restricted IFC entities and properties when serving requests to users lacking appropriate clearance[^2].           | Redacted elements are omitted from the geometry stream and web viewer display[^2].                |
| **FR-05.3**    | Cryptographic Audit Ledger  | All user actions, validations, state transitions, and file downloads must be written to an append-only audit ledger with SHA-256 hash chaining[^3]. | System verifies cryptographic hash chain integrity periodically via automated background workers. |

### **CDE Interoperability and API Conformance (FR-06)**

| Requirement ID | Requirement Specification          | Verification Criteria and Logic                                                                                                              | Implementation Target                                                                      |
| :------------- | :--------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **FR-06.1**    | openCDE Foundation API Conformance | Platform must expose standard openCDE Foundation v1.0 endpoints (/api/cde/versions, /api/cde/profile) with OAuth2 Bearer authentication[^2]. | External CDE clients query server capabilities and authenticate via OAuth2 token flow[^2]. |
| **FR-06.2**    | openCDE Documents Integration      | System must implement openCDE Documents API endpoints, supporting document synchronization via HTTP ETag change detection[^2].               | External systems poll /api/cde/documents with ETags; unchanged assets return HTTP 304[^2]. |
| **FR-06.3**    | BCF REST API v3.0 Conformance      | System must implement standard BCF REST API endpoints supporting bi-directional topic creation, synchronization, and commenting[^2].         | Design authoring tools synchronize clash issues directly via REST endpoints[^2].           |

## **Non-Functional Requirements and Operational Constraints**

To ensure reliable performance in production environments handling large OpenBIM datasets, BIM-Guard must operate within strict non-functional performance boundaries.

| Metric Classification                | Target Performance Threshold   | Measurement Conditions and Verification Method                                                                                        |
| :----------------------------------- | :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Syntactic Parsing Latency**        | **<= 5** seconds               | Parsing and validating ISO 10303-21 STEP physical syntax on IFC models up to 250 MB in file size[^2].                                 |
| **IDS 1.0 Execution Latency**        | **<= 30** seconds              | Auditing an IFC model containing up to 100,000 entities against an IDS XML rule file with 50 distinct requirement facets[^2].         |
| **Concurrent Processing Throughput** | **>= 10** concurrent pipelines | Executing full four-tier validation pipelines simultaneously across distributed Celery/Redis worker nodes without HTTP timeouts.      |
| **Viewport Rendering Frame Rate**    | **>= 30** frames per second    | Navigating, sectioning, and highlighting clash viewpoints in the ThatOpenCompany Web-IFC viewer on standard desktop hardware[^2].     |
| **API Response Latency**             | **<= 200** milliseconds        | Serving metadata queries, CDE state transitions, and openCDE document manifests under a sustained load of 50 requests per second[^2]. |
| **Service Availability**             | 99.9% uptime                   | Application gateway and CDE services uptime measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance[^2].                                    |
| **Data Recovery Objectives**         | RPO <= 15 min; RTO <= 4 hours  | Point-in-time recovery for Supabase PostgreSQL transactional databases and associated object storage[^2].                             |

Processing large IFC models generates substantial computational overhead[^2]. The platform's asynchronous pipeline must prevent worker processes from exhausting system resources during model ingestion[^2]. Tasks must run in isolated containerized environments with hard memory limits (8 GB RAM per worker). If a file exceeds the allocated memory ceiling or experiences a processing error during geometric parsing, the worker must cleanly terminate the task, reset the container status to EVALUATION_FAILED, release all file descriptors, and record a diagnostic log to the audit journal[^2].

Security configurations require that all network communication across external clients, the FastAPI application gateway, and backend database instances enforce TLS 1.3 encryption. Files stored in Supabase storage buckets must be encrypted at rest using AES-256[^2].

## **OpenBIM Interoperability and Ecosystem Integration**

BIM-Guard operates within the wider buildingSMART OpenBIM software ecosystem[^2]. Full ISO 19650 compliance requires seamless data exchange with third-party common data environments, computer-aided design (CAD) software, and Building Information Modeling authoring platforms without vendor lock-in[^4].

To maintain an open architecture, BIM-Guard implements three standardized buildingSMART interface protocols: the openCDE Foundation API, the openCDE Documents API, and the BCF REST API v3.0[^2]. Rather than forcing design teams to manually export and upload files through web forms, external CDEs (such as Autodesk Construction Cloud, Trimble Connect, and Dalux) can connect directly to BIM-Guard using openCDE service hooks[^2]. When an information container is committed to an external project repository, an automated webhook notifies BIM-Guard's /api/cde/documents endpoint[^2]. The platform ingests the container, executes the four-tier verification and validation pipeline, and returns the compliance disposition alongside detailed BCF issue packages directly to the host platform[^2].

| Protocol Name                     | Standard Version      | Implemented Endpoints                                                | Operational Function                                                                                            |
| :-------------------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **openCDE Foundation API**        | v1.0[^8]              | /api/cde/versions /api/cde/profile                                   | Discovers service capabilities, supported API versions, and validates user authentication profiles[^2].         |
| **openCDE Documents API**         | v1.0[^8]              | /api/cde/documents /api/cde/documents/{id}/download                  | Handles document exchanges, container metadata synchronization, and HTTP 304 ETag caching[^2].                  |
| **buildingSMART BCF REST API**    | v3.0[^8]              | /api/bcf/v3.0/projects /api/bcf/v3.0/topics /api/bcf/v3.0/viewpoints | Synchronizes compliance issues, clash viewpoints, camera angles, and resolution comments with design tools[^2]. |
| **buildingSMART Data Dictionary** | REST / GraphQL v1[^8] | External outgoing client query service to api.bsdd.buildingsmart.org | Validates classification properties, property set domains, and standard measurement units[^2].                  |

The bSDD integration client acts as a semantic bridge, resolving project-specific classifications and property names against international data dictionaries[^2]. During Tier 3 semantic validation, the engine extracts classification URIs declared in the IFC model (for example, Uniclass 2015 Pr or EF tables) and verifies them against the official bSDD schema[^2]. To maintain operational reliability during network interruptions, BIM-Guard utilizes a local cache of standard classification systems[^2].

The BCF REST API v3.0 interface allows architectural and MEP design teams working in applications like Revit, ArchiCAD, or BlenderBIM to query validation issues directly within their design viewports[^2]. When a design model is flagged for a code violation—such as an uninsulated pipe crossing a seismic joint (GC-001) or incompatible metals causing galvanic corrosion risks (CC-001)—the designer receives an actionable BCF topic[^2]. Clicking the topic navigates the authoring software's camera to the exact spatial coordinate, isolates the affected components using their IFC GUIDs, and displays the corrective measures required to satisfy the project information requirements[^2].

## **Strategic Implementation Conclusions**

Achieving ISO 19650 compliance elevates BIM-Guard from an automated compliance checking script into an enterprise-grade digital information gatekeeper[^2]. By decoupling physical file names from mutable operational metadata[^11], enforcing a four-state CDE workflow machine through database-level triggers[^2], deploying a four-tier automated exchange verification pipeline[^2], and incorporating security-minded information triage and dynamic redaction[^9], the platform guarantees that digital assets remain verifiable, legally defensible, and reliable throughout the project lifecycle[^3].

The operational realization of this specification follows a phased implementation path: The initial phase focuses on the Supabase PostgreSQL database architecture, deploying migration scripts that establish the decoupled container metadata schema, CDE state machine enums, and row-level security policies[^2]. The second phase delivers the core ingestion gatekeeper, activating the 7-field National Annex file naming parser and the automated buildingSMART IDS 1.0 validation engine[^8]. The third phase deploys the openCDE Foundation, Documents, and BCF REST API v3.0 endpoints, enabling bi-directional federation with external CDE platforms and design authoring tools[^2]. The final phase integrates ISO 19650-5 security controls, implementing dynamic IFC geometry and semantic entity redaction alongside cryptographic audit chaining[^9].

By completing this technical implementation, BIM-Guard establishes an automated OpenBIM delivery pipeline that minimizes manual review overhead, eliminates versioning ambiguity, and enforces technical, operational, and security compliance across all asset delivery milestones[^3].
```

```text
    Creates a card footer

- `def CardContainer(*c, **kwargs)`
    Creates a card container

- `def Card(*c, **kwargs)`
    Creates a Card with a header, body, and footer

- `class TableT(Enum)`
    Members: divider, striped, hover, sm, lg, justify, middle, responsive


- `def Table(*c, **kwargs)`
    Creates a table

- `def TableFromLists(header_data, body_data, footer_data, header_cell_render, body_cell_render, footer_cell_render, cls, sortable, **kwargs)`
    Creates a Table from a list of header data and a list of lists of body data

- `def TableFromDicts(header_data, body_data, footer_data, header_cell_render, body_cell_render, footer_cell_render, cls, sortable, **kwargs)`
    Creates a Table from a list of header data and a list of dicts of body data

- `def apply_classes(html_str, class_map, class_map_mods)`
    Apply classes to html string

- `class FrankenRenderer`
    Custom renderer for Franken UI that handles image paths

    - `def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs)`
    - `def render_image(self, token)`
        Modify image paths if they're relative and self.img_dir is specified


- `def render_md(md_content, class_map, class_map_mods, img_dir, renderer)`
    Renders markdown using mistletoe and lxml with custom image handling

- `def ThemePicker(color, radii, shadows, font, mode, cls, custom_themes)`
    Theme picker component with configurable sections

- `def LightboxContainer(*lightboxitem, **kwargs)`
    Lightbox container that will hold `LightboxItems`

- `def LightboxItem(*c, **kwargs)`
    Anchor tag with appropriate structure to go inside a `LightBoxContainer`

- `def ApexChart(**kws)`
    Apex chart component

- `def ScrollSpy(headings, target_sel, offset, nav_id, smooth_scroll, auto_scroll, cls, **kwargs)`
    Standalone Scrollspy nav menu, mapping heading tags from target into link

- `def LoaderButton(*c, **kwargs)`
    A button that displays a loading spinner when an HTMX request is in flight

- `def ToggleBtn(*c, **kwargs)`
    Styled toggle button component, acts like a switch
```
````text
</doc></api reference><examples><doc title="Playground" desc="FrankenUI Playground Example built with MonsterUI (original design by ShadCN)">"""FrankenUI Playground Example built with MonsterUI (original design by ShadCN)"""

from fasthtml.common import *
from monsterui.all import *
from fasthtml.svg import *

app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=Theme.blue.headers())

preset_options = ["Grammatical Standard English", "Summarize for a 2nd grader",
        "Text to command","Q&A","English to other languages","Parse unstructured data",
        "Classification","Natural language to Python","Explain code","Chat","More examples"]

def playground_navbar():
    save_modal = Modal(
        ModalTitle("Save preset"),
        P("This will save the current playground state as a preset which you can access later or share with others.",cls=("mt-1.5", TextPresets.muted_sm)),
        LabelInput("Name",        id="name"), 
        LabelInput("Description", id="description"),
        ModalCloseButton("Save", cls=ButtonT.primary),
        id="save")
    
    share_dd = Div(cls="space-y-6 p-4")(
        H3("Share preset"),
        P("Anyone who has this link and an OpenAI account will be able to view this.", cls=TextPresets.muted_sm),
        Div(Input(value="https://platform.openai.com/playground/p/7bbKYQvsVkNmVb8NGcdUOLae?model=text-davinci-003", readonly=True),
            Button(UkIcon('copy'), cls=(ButtonT.primary, "uk-drop-close",'mt-4'))))

    rnav = (
        Select(*Options(*preset_options), name='preset', optgroup_label="Examples",
                 placeholder='Load a preset', searchable=True, cls='h-9 w-[200px] lg:w-[300px]'),
        Button("Save",         cls=ButtonT.secondary, data_uk_toggle="#save"),save_modal,
        Button("View Code",    cls=ButtonT.secondary),
        Button("Share",        cls=ButtonT.secondary),DropDownNavContainer(share_dd),
        Button(UkIcon(icon="ellipsis"), cls=ButtonT.secondary),
        DropDownNavContainer(
            Li(A("Content filter preferences")),
            NavDividerLi(),
            Li(A("Delete preset", cls="text-destructive")),
        uk_dropdown="mode: click"))
    
    return NavBar(*rnav, brand=H4('Playground'))

rsidebar = NavContainer(
    Select(
        Optgroup(map(Option,("text-davinci-003", "text-curie-001", "text-babbage-001", "text-ada-001")),label='GPT-3'),
        Optgroup(map(Option,("code-davinci-002", "code-cushman-001")),label='Codex'),
        label="Model",
        searchable=True),
    LabelRange(label='Temperature', value='12'),
    LabelRange(label='Maximum Length', value='80'),
    LabelRange(label='Top P', value='40'),
    cls='space-y-6 mt-8')

@rt
def index(): 
    navbar = playground_navbar()
    main_content = Div(
        Div(cls="flex-1")(
            Textarea(cls="uk-textarea h-full p-4", placeholder="Write a tagline for an ice cream shop")),
            cls="flex h-[700px] p-8 w-4/5")
    
    bottom_buttons = Div(
        Button("Submit", cls=ButtonT.primary),
        Button(UkIcon(icon="history"), cls=ButtonT.secondary),
        cls="flex gap-x-2")
    
    return Title("Playground Example"),Div(navbar, Div(cls="flex w-full")(main_content, rsidebar), bottom_buttons)

serve()</doc><doc title="Tasks" desc="FrankenUI Tasks Example built with MonsterUI (original design by ShadCN)">"""FrankenUI Tasks Example built with MonsterUI (original design by ShadCN)"""

from fasthtml.common import *
from monsterui.all import *
from fasthtml.svg import *
import json

app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=Theme.blue.headers())

def LAlignedCheckTxt(txt): return DivLAligned(UkIcon(icon='check'), P(txt, cls=TextPresets.muted_sm))

with open('data_/status_list.json', 'r') as f: data     = json.load(f)
with open('data_/statuses.json',    'r') as f: statuses = json.load(f)

def _create_tbl_data(d):
    return {'Done': d['selected'], 'Task': d['id'], 'Title': d['title'],
            'Status'  : d['status'], 'Priority': d['priority'] }

data = [_create_tbl_data(d)  for d in data]
page_size = 15
current_page = 0
paginated_data = data[current_page*page_size:(current_page+1)*page_size]

priority_dd = [{'priority': "low", 'count': 36 }, {'priority': "medium", 'count': 33 }, {'priority': "high", 'count': 31 }]

status_dd = [{'status': "backlog", 'count': 21 },{'status': "todo", 'count': 21 },{'status': "progress", 'count': 20 },{'status': "done",'count': 19 },{'status': "cancelled", 'count': 19 }]

def create_hotkey_li(hotkey): return NavCloseLi(A(DivFullySpaced(hotkey[0], Span(hotkey[1], cls=TextPresets.muted_sm))))

hotkeys_a = (('Profile','⇧⌘P'),('Billing','⌘B'),('Settings','⌘S'),('New Team',''))
hotkeys_b = (('Logout',''), )

avatar_opts = DropDownNavContainer(
    NavHeaderLi(P('sveltecult'),NavSubtitle('leader@sveltecult.com')),
    NavDividerLi(),
    *map(create_hotkey_li, hotkeys_a),
    NavDividerLi(),
    *map(create_hotkey_li, hotkeys_b),)

def CreateTaskModal():
    return Modal(
        Div(cls='p-6')(
            ModalTitle('Create Task'),
            P('Fill out the information below to create a new task', cls=TextPresets.muted_sm),
            Br(),
            Form(cls='space-y-6')(
                Grid(Div(Select(*map(Option,('Documentation', 'Bug', 'Feature')), label='Task Type', id='task_type')),
                     Div(Select(*map(Option,('In Progress', 'Backlog', 'Todo', 'Cancelled', 'Done')), label='Status', id='task_status')),
                     Div(Select(*map(Option, ('Low', 'Medium', 'High')), label='Priority', id='task_priority'))),
                TextArea(label='Title', placeholder='Please describe the task that needs to be completed'),
                DivRAligned(
                    ModalCloseButton('Cancel', cls=ButtonT.ghost),
                    ModalCloseButton('Submit', cls=ButtonT.primary),
                    cls='space-x-5'))),
        id='TaskForm')

page_heading = DivFullySpaced(cls='space-y-2')(
            Div(cls='space-y-2')(
                H2('Welcome back!'),P("Here's a list of your tasks for this month!", cls=TextPresets.muted_sm)),
            Div(DiceBearAvatar("sveltcult",8,8),avatar_opts))

table_controls =(Input(cls='w-[250px]',placeholder='Filter task'),
     Button("Status"),
     DropDownNavContainer(map(NavCloseLi,[A(DivFullySpaced(P(a['status']), P(a['count'])),cls='capitalize') for a in status_dd])), 
     Button("Priority"),
     DropDownNavContainer(map(NavCloseLi,[A(DivFullySpaced(LAlignedCheckTxt(a['priority']), a['count']),cls='capitalize') for a in priority_dd])),
     Button("View"),
     DropDownNavContainer(map(NavCloseLi,[A(LAlignedCheckTxt(o)) for o in ['Title','Status','Priority']])),
     Button('Create Task',cls=(ButtonT.primary, TextPresets.bold_sm), data_uk_toggle="target: #TaskForm"))

def task_dropdown():
    return Div(Button(UkIcon('ellipsis')),
               DropDownNavContainer(
                   map(NavCloseLi,[
                       *map(A,('Edit', 'Make a copy', 'Favorite')),
                        A(DivFullySpaced(*[P(o, cls=TextPresets.muted_sm) for o in ('Delete', '⌘⌫')]))])))
def header_render(col):
    match col:
        case "Done":    return Th(CheckboxX(), shrink=True)
        case 'Actions': return Th("",          shrink=True)
        case _:         return Th(col,         expand=True)

def cell_render(col, val):
    def _Td(*args,cls='', **kwargs): return Td(*args, cls=f'p-2 {cls}',**kwargs)
    match col:
        case "Done": return _Td(shrink=True)(CheckboxX(selected=val))
        case "Task":  return _Td(val, cls='uk-visible@s')  # Hide on small screens
        case "Title": return _Td(val, cls='font-medium', expand=True)
        case "Status" | "Priority": return _Td(cls='uk-visible@m uk-text-nowrap capitalize')(Span(val))
        case "Actions": return _Td(task_dropdown(), shrink=True)
        case _: raise ValueError(f"Unknown column: {col}")

task_columns = ["Done", 'Task', 'Title', 'Status', 'Priority', 'Actions']

tasks_table = Div(cls='mt-4')(
    TableFromDicts(
        header_data=task_columns,
        body_data=paginated_data,
        body_cell_render=cell_render,
        header_cell_render=header_render,
        sortable=True,
        cls=(TableT.responsive, TableT.sm, TableT.divider)))


def footer():
    total_pages = (len(data) + page_size - 1) // page_size
    return DivFullySpaced(
        Div('1 of 100 row(s) selected.', cls=TextPresets.muted_sm),
        DivLAligned(
            DivCentered(f'Page {current_page + 1} of {total_pages}', cls=TextT.sm),
            DivLAligned(*[UkIconLink(icon=i,  button=True) for i in ('chevrons-left', 'chevron-left', 'chevron-right', 'chevrons-right')])))

tasks_ui = Div(DivFullySpaced(DivLAligned(table_controls), cls='mt-8'), tasks_table, footer())

@rt
def index(): return Container(page_heading, tasks_ui, CreateTaskModal())

serve()</doc><doc title="Ticket" desc="MonsterUI Help Desk Example - Professional Dashboard with DaisyUI components">"""MonsterUI Help Desk Example - Professional Dashboard with DaisyUI components"""
from fasthtml.common import *
from monsterui.all import *
from datetime import datetime

app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=Theme.blue.headers(daisy=True))

def TicketSteps(step):
    return Steps(
        LiStep("Submitted", data_content="📝",
               cls=StepT.success if step > 0 else StepT.primary if step == 0 else StepT.neutral),
        LiStep("In Review", data_content="🔎",
               cls=StepT.success if step > 1 else StepT.primary if step == 1 else StepT.neutral),
        LiStep("Processing", data_content="⚙️",
               cls=StepT.success if step > 2 else StepT.primary if step == 2 else StepT.neutral),
        LiStep("Resolved", data_content="✅",
               cls=StepT.success if step > 3 else StepT.primary if step == 3 else StepT.neutral),
        cls="w-full")

def StatusBadge(status):
    styles = {'high': AlertT.error, 'medium': AlertT.warning,'low': AlertT.info}
    alert_type = styles.get(status, AlertT.info)
    return Alert(f"{status.title()} Priority", cls=(alert_type,"w-32 shadow-sm"))

def TicketCard(id, title, description, status, step, department):
    return Card(
        CardHeader(
            DivFullySpaced(
                Div(H3(f"#{id}", cls=TextT.muted), 
                    H4(title), 
                    cls='space-y-2'),
                StatusBadge(status))),
        CardBody(
            P(description, cls=(TextT.muted, "mb-6")),
            DividerSplit(cls="my-6"),
            TicketSteps(step),
            DividerSplit(cls="my-6"), 
            DivFullySpaced(
                Div(Strong("Department"),
                    P(department),
                    cls=('space-y-3', TextPresets.muted_sm)),
                Div(Strong("Last Updated"),
                    P(Time(datetime.now().strftime('%b %d, %H:%M'))),
                    cls=('space-y-3', TextPresets.muted_sm)),
                Button("View Details", cls=ButtonT.primary),
                cls='mt-6')),
        cls=CardT.hover)

def NewTicketModal():
    return Modal(
        ModalHeader(H3("Create New Support Ticket")),
        ModalBody(
            Alert(
                DivLAligned(UkIcon("info"), Span("Please provide as much detail as possible to help us assist you quickly.")),
                cls=(AlertT.info,"mb-4")),
            Form(
                Grid(LabelInput("Title", id="title", placeholder="Brief description of your issue"),
                     LabelSelect(Options("IT Support", "HR", "Facilities", "Finance"), label="Department", id="department")),
                LabelSelect(Options("Low", "Medium", "High"), label="Priority Level",  id="priority"),
                LabelTextArea("Description", id="description", placeholder="Please provide detailed information about your issue"),
                DivRAligned(
                    Button("Cancel", cls=ButtonT.ghost, data_uk_toggle="target: #new-ticket"),
                    Button(Loading(cls=LoadingT.spinner), "Submit Ticket", cls=ButtonT.primary, data_uk_toggle="target: #success-toast; target: #new-ticket")),
                cls='space-y-8')),
            id="new-ticket")

@rt
def index():
    tickets = [
        {'id': "TK-1001", 'title': "Cloud Storage Access Error", 
         'description': "Unable to access cloud storage with persistent authorization errors. Multiple users affected across marketing department.",
         'status': 'high', 'step': 2, 'department': 'IT Support'},
        {'id': "TK-1002", 'title': "Email Integration Issue", 
         'description': "Exchange server not syncing with mobile devices. Affecting external client communications.",
         'status': 'medium', 'step': 1, 'department': 'IT Support'},
        {'id': "TK-1003", 'title': "Office Equipment Setup", 
         'description': "New department printer needs configuration and network integration. Required for upcoming client presentation.",
         'status': 'low', 'step': 0, 'department': 'Facilities'}
    ]

    return Title("Help Desk Dashboard"), Container(
        Section(
            DivFullySpaced(
                H2("Active Tickets"),
                Button(UkIcon("plus-circle", cls="mr-2"), "New Ticket", cls=ButtonT.primary, data_uk_toggle="target: #new-ticket"),
                cls='mb-8'),
            Grid(*[TicketCard(**ticket) for ticket in tickets], cols=1),
            cls="my-6"),
        NewTicketModal(),
        Toast(DivLAligned(UkIcon('check-circle', cls='mr-2'), "Ticket submitted successfully! Our team will review it shortly."), id="success-toast", alert_cls=AlertT.success, cls=(ToastHT.end, ToastVT.bottom)),
        Loading(htmx_indicator=True, type=LoadingT.dots, cls="fixed top-0 right-0 m-4"),
        cls="mx-auto max-w-7xl"
    )
````
